A gate rising on a channel puts that channel's pitch into the note list, and its falling takes the note out again unless hold is on
A voltage carried along with the note played on the same channel and passed on at the CV1 output, as the S&H switch for CV1 sets
A voltage carried along with the note played on the same channel and passed on at the CV2 output, as the S&H switch for CV2 sets
Chooses what the CV1 output carries: I keeps the CV1 voltage sampled as the note was played, C passes the present voltage of the note's own input channel, and O samples it on the output clock
Chooses what the CV2 output carries: I keeps the CV2 voltage sampled as the note was played, C passes the present voltage of the note's own input channel, and O samples it on the output clock
Passes the gates of the Clock input on each channel while there are notes in the list
The pitch of the note that channel's arpeggio is playing, at a volt per octave
The voltage stored or sampled for the note that channel is playing, as the CV1 switch sets
The voltage stored or sampled for the note that channel is playing, as the CV2 switch sets
Note — with a monophonic Gate and V/Oct pair and hold in use, incoming notes are spread across the channels in turn, which lets patterns be entered from a sequencer
Note — nothing comes out until a gate at the Gate input puts a note into the list and a clock at the Clock input steps the arpeggio; with Clock unpatched the outputs stay where they are
Arpeggiator.notes: Input 4 (CV 3) and outputs 4 and 5 are declared in the code but have no jack on the panel, so they are left untagged. The note-input polyphony is worked out as the smaller of the V/Oct channel count and the Gate OUTPUT channel count, which follows the Clock input, so a patch with fewer Clock channels than played notes reads fewer notes than are being played. The CV 3 input and the CV 3 output are configured on the panel but nothing in the installed v2.0.3 source reads or writes either of them.
